title: Annie: From Comic Strip to Broadway
description: A stray dog, a billionaire, and a president who learns to sing—five steps into Broadway's favorite orphan.
imageHint: Broadway stage with red curly-haired girl in red dress, NYC skyline backdrop, golden spotlight

questions.question: Little orphan Annie promises that "the sun'll come out" in her signature song. What is it called?
acceptedAnswers: the sun will come out tomorrow
questions.explanation: Lyricist Martin Charnin bought a Little Orphan Annie book as a Christmas gift in 1970, read it instead of wrapping it, and set out to get the rights. The friend never got the book.

questions.question: Annie sings Tomorrow to a stray mutt running from the dogcatcher, then names him on the spot to fool a cop. What is his name?
questions.explanation: The original Sandy was a shelter mutt found by William Berloni, a 19-year-old apprentice promised his Equity card for it. That Sandy never missed a performance.

questions.question: Annie and Sandy end up in the Manhattan mansion of which billionaire?
questions.explanation: The decoys are all from the show: Bert Healy is the radio host, Rooster is Miss Hannigan's con-man brother, and Mr. Bundles is the laundry man.

questions.question: Warbucks takes Annie to the White House, where she gets a gloomy cabinet singing Tomorrow. Which president leads them?
questions.explanation: In the musical, Annie's optimism inspires FDR and his cabinet to dream up the New Deal. Earlier, the residents of a shantytown sing a sarcastic thank-you to Herbert Hoover.

questions.question: Roosevelt gets the reprise, but in Harold Gray's comic strip, Annie had a famous exclamation of her own. What was it?
questions.explanation: The New York Times noticed in 1977 that the musical keeps just one "Leapin' Lizards" and drops her other favorite, "Gloryosky," entirely.

easterEgg.title: Before Carrie Bradshaw
easterEgg.text: Sarah Jessica Parker took over the title role during the original Broadway run. Molly Ringwald and Alyssa Milano both played orphans in the show, and Jane Lynch made her Broadway debut as Miss Hannigan.
